title: Comparison of 3D GPR Migration Algorithms for Resolving Closely Spaced Parallel Pipes at Shallow Depth

record.title: Comparison of 3D GPR Migration Algorithms for Resolving Closely Spaced Parallel Pipes at Shallow Depth
record.abstract: When two pipes run in parallel at separation distances below the Rayleigh resolution limit of the antenna in use, standard B-scan interpretation underestimates pipe count and misestimates lateral positions. This study compared Kirchhoff migration, frequency-wavenumber migration and reverse-time migration applied to synthetic C-scan volumes and to field data collected over a test trench containing three 63 mm PE pipes at 0.7 m depth with 120 mm centre-to-centre spacing. The 900 MHz antenna was traversed in a 0.05 m × 0.05 m grid pattern over a 2 m × 2 m aperture. Kirchhoff migration separated the two outer pipes in 78% of synthetic realisations but failed to resolve the central pipe. Frequency-wavenumber migration resolved all three pipes in 91% of realisations and produced lateral position errors below 25 mm. Field validation using a reference frame showed mean lateral positioning error of 21 mm for frequency-wavenumber versus 54 mm for Kirchhoff. Processing time remained tractable on standard desktop hardware at under 90 seconds per C-scan volume.
